messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler failed to increase GPU pool in eu-west-1 (scale_error: provider-rate-limit). queue_length for model-redwood-1 exceeded 18k, throttling users. See /alerts/3790012345
maria: saw that. customers hitting 429s on hosted API, some Dedicated tenants seeing increased latency too.
oncall_ek: I'm onpager. starting triage — grabbing dashboards and the autoscale logs.
sam_k: metric links: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/scale/queue?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1
sam_k: queue growth started ~12:03 UTC, steep slope at 12:09.
kevin: provider responded with 429/QuotaExceeded around the same time, repeated for 3 minutes then backoff retries.
jess: any active maintenance or region incidents on provider side? I don't see scheduled changes.
infra-bot: Autoscaler error log snapshot:
```
2026-03-15T12:09:11Z ERROR scaler: scaleup failed: provider api error: 429 too many requests
2026-03-15T12:09:12Z WARN scaler: backoff 30s
2026-03-15T12:10:00Z ERROR scaler: scaleup failed: limit reached for account
```
maria: this looks like provider quota hit + our scale limits. can we open a delay-mitigation? i.e. early shedding or fallback.
oncall_ek: mitigation plan proposals:
  1) enable model-fallback to smaller variant (model-redwood-1-quant) for non-enterprise traffic
  2) raise autoscaler max instances temporarily in eu-west-1 (if provider allows)
  3) rate-limit /burst routes and enable 503-with-retry for some low-priority tenants
  4) if needed, manual provisioning request to provider support
sam_k: I can flip the fallback routing now via routing flag `enable_fallback_eu_west`.
kevin: provisioning requests will take 30-45m. provider quota increase might be too slow for immediate mitigation.
jess: agree. option 1 + 3 is fastest.
maria: @sam_k go for fallback now. post what you changed.
sam_k: toggled fallback in route config (deploy 2s). command:
```
redwoodctl routes update --region eu-west-1 --set enable_fallback=true --target model-redwood-1-quant
```
sam_k: confirmed: 60% of new requests are now routed to quant variant. queue drain started in 2m.
oncall_ek: starting to rate-limit noisy tenants. @support-liaison can you surface which tenants had errors to CS?
support-liaison: will compile list and send email draft to affected customers. rough count: ~14 small tenants, 2 medium (non-enterprise).
kevin: we still have some throttling at autoscaler layer because of provider rate-limit responses. can we temporarily lower scale-down aggressiveness to keep instances warm?
infra-bot: set autoscaler min_replicas from 2 -> 6 in eu-west-1 to avoid churn.
infra-bot: command executed: `infractl autoscaler patch --region eu-west-1 --min 6`
jess: good call.
oncall_ek: monitoring: queue length peaked at 18.4k, now down to 3.2k after fallback + rate limits. 429s down from 8% -> 0.6% in last 6m.
maria: part of the traffic that hit the quant variant shows slight latency improvement, cost up a bit but acceptable for mitigation.
kevin: we should also check eviction behavior: did any pods get preempted causing extra scale events?
sam_k: checking node events. I see a burst of preemptions around 12:08 correlated with provider-side maintenance in AZ-a.
jess: okay. immediate next steps so we can close pager:
  - keep fallback enabled for 30m and observe
  - keep min_replicas=6 for 45m
  - support-liaison to send customer notification template (prepared)
  - infra to submit quota increase request to provider and escalate
oncall_ek: I'll hand off to night oncall in 35m if stable. @maria want to own postmortem?
maria: I can lead the postmortem, will coordinate with infra and provider contact. please add logs/evt slices.
support-liaison: posting customer note draft now in #support (copy pasted):
```
Hi — 
We saw transient errors for some API requests (429) in eu-west-1 today due to capacity provisioning delays. We enabled an automated fallback to a quantized model to restore service and rate-limited non-critical routes. Impact: intermittent 429s for ~20 minutes for select tenants. If you need further details contact support@redwood.ai
```
kevin: assigning infra action: open ticket with provider with reference 3790012345, request quota bump and preemption root cause.
infra-bot: ticket created: PROVIDER-89234, priority P2.
oncall_ek: summary for postmortem notes (raw):
  - trigger: provider rate-limits and preemptions prevented autoscaler from bringing up nodes
  - impact: queue growth -> API 429s for ~20m, elevated latency for Dedicated routes
  - mitigation: enable model fallback, increase min_replicas, rate-limit noisy tenants
  - immediate followups: provider quota request, revisit autoscaler retry/backoff, add observability for preemption spikes
jess: suggest action item: add emergency fallback toggle to console (one-click) + audit who can flip.
maria: added to action items. also want an evaluation: quantify quality delta between base vs quantized model for affected tenants.
sam_k: logging note: we'll snapshot KV cache pressure and token loss metrics for the 12:00-12:30 window.
support-liaison: customer messages sent. one medium tenant replied asking for postmortem once done.
oncall_ek: closing update: system stable, queue back to normal 250 requests. marking pager resolved but keeping channel open for postmortem details.
maria: thanks all. postmortem doc will be in docs/incidents/3790012345-autoscaler-lockup-postmortem.md and I'll ping owners. main owners: maria (lead), kevin (infra), sam_k (runtime), jess (product).
kevin: immediate TODOs:
  - [ ] escalate quota (PROVIDER-89234) — kevin
  - [ ] add preemption spike alert to Grafana — sam_k
  - [ ] console fallback button design spec — jess
  - [ ] post-incident customer outreach follow-up — support-liaison
maria: marking this thread as handoff to postmortem. thanks everyone :pray:
infra-bot: incident closed by oncall_ek at 12:21 UTC. logs archived to /incidents/3790012345/logs.tar.gz
